name: desire for territory
description: Wanting to reserve physical or social assets for yourself or important others. You may plan to do this through trade or by force.
perceptions: I need a certain type of asset to be safe and satisfied.

comparisons.description: Territory is a special form of wealth. By itself, a physical space may not be valuable, but it provides a basis for wealth creation through farming, commerce, meeting space, etc. Staking out physical territory is deeply rooted behavior seen in many animals, and many people feel attachment to physical spaces.

variations.name: defending home territory
variations.description: Wanting to defend a particular physical or social space as your own. To have enough resources to safely survive, many animals mark their territory and are willing to fight to defend it.

commentaries.quote: Social assets can be territory as well, like being the sales rep for an important client or a top media influencer in a lucrative category. Of course 'attacking' and 'defending' may look different for social assets than for physical assets.
Being told to pick up sticks in your parent's yard feels a lot different than picking up sticks in your own yard.

Protect your Territory; your dreams, goals, interests, family, friends, everything that in some way have become your essence, protect and nurture it through the good and the bad times. Give no one the power to decide who or what's in or out. Make your territory yours. Mark it in linnings of brimming coals if you may.

Owning land provides a fundamental sense of stability and security, essential for mental well-being. It offers a permanent place in the world, a sanctuary where one can feel safe and grounded. This stability often translates into reduced stress and anxiety, providing a solid foundation for mental health.
Owning land is like owning the ocean, or the air. no one owns land.

Some people extol the virtues of land ownership. Others resent the concept that immortal land can 'belong' to short-lived creatures like humans. They're both right. Think of 'owning' real estate more as a legal right against other people to what happens on a tiny part of the earth. Be good to the land, nurture it, and in return, it will sustain you. Soon enough, you will trade the legal paper to the next human for money. And so through the ages.
